notes:
Company background: CompileX builds an enterprise IDE copilot used by mid-to-large engineering teams (editor plugins, CI-integrations). Looking to replace a patchwork of hosted endpoints with a predictable dedicated runtime for peak developer hours.

Primary ask: Dedicated capacity sized for peak dev hours (workday 09:00-18:00 PST), support for burst to cover async spikes (code-completion floods at standups/merge waves). Must guarantee low tail latency for inline completions.

Technical requirements (from SE call):
- Workload: low-latency streaming for inline completions + chat-assisted code explainers; heavy token mix of short completions (<= 64 tokens) + occasional longer summarizations.
- Targets: median completion RTT < 150ms; first-token streaming < 50ms; p50/p95 throughput for 300 concurrent dev sessions, headroom for 2x burst to 700 concurrent.
- Model requirements: pinning by app-version; primary model = CodeLlama-34B-optimized or quantized Llama2 variant; fallback to 7B quantized during saturation. Need per-route model mapping (release channels dev/stable).
- KV/prefix caching: reuse completion context across quick edits; per-user KV isolation.
- Integration: VSCode extension uses Redwood SDK + streaming websocket for first-token; also CI lint/rerank endpoints (reranking less latency-sensitive).
- Deployment: prefer Dedicated with VPC peering; must support AWS KMS for key management; data residency US-only for now.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II in progress; need audit_logging and retention controls; legal needs DPA + security appendix.

POC plan: 4-week dedicated POC. Week1 baseline perf tests (300 concurrent sessions simulated), Week2 model pinning + canary switch, Week3 burst ramp tests, Week4 finalize SLA/cost. Success metrics: sustained p95 latency < 250ms under baseline, graceful fallback under burst, stable cost within estimate.

Quotes / call snippets: "We can't tolerate unpredictable throttling — peak hours must be guaranteed or developers will turn off the plugin." — CTO Alex Ramesh.

Risks & notes: network/VPC approval on their side is slow; security team asked for runtime attestation and KMS flow diagrams (we provided draft), want clearer burst billing examples (per-hour vs per-peak).

Next steps (internal): provide sample Dedicated pool configuration (GPU profile + instance counts) and annotated cost breakdown for baseline + 2x burst; SE to run spike test config on sandbox cluster; legal to send DPA template.
